title: Time-Series Foundation Models
interviewAnswer: Time-series foundation models pretrain on large collections of sequences and adapt or zero-shot forecast new series. They can reduce per-series modeling work, but still need comparison with strong naive/statistical baselines and careful domain-shift evaluation.
why: Foundation-model ideas have moved into forecasting and are increasingly relevant to modern applied ML.
intuition: Instead of fitting one model from scratch for each SKU or sensor, pretrain broad temporal patterns and adapt to new series.
deepDive: Architectures vary—tokenized patches, transformers or pretrained probabilistic decoders—but evaluation must preserve time order and account for horizon, scale and domain mismatch.
commonMistakes: Assuming a foundation model automatically beats statistical forecasting.
Evaluating with random splits or mismatched horizons.
followUps: How would you fine-tune without leakage?
production: Benchmark latency/cost, calibration and per-segment accuracy; keep simple fallback forecasts for failure cases.
workedExample: A global pretrained model can forecast a newly introduced product with little history, then be compared against seasonal-naive/ETS baselines.
